correctness.rationale: The exact normal-defect identity follows by direct differentiation and proves the published nullcline is not invariant. The only complete orbit on that nullcline is the equilibrium. For fixed \(\alpha>0\), the \(\varepsilon^{-1}\) formulation has normally hyperbolic attracting critical manifold \(z=0\) on a compact annulus. Fenichel persistence gives a true slow manifold with expansion \(z=\varepsilon^{-1}(y^2-1)+2xy/(\alpha\varepsilon^2)+O(\varepsilon^{-3})\). First-order averaging of the reduced flow gives radial field \(r(4-3r^2)/8\) with a simple attracting zero at \(r=2/\sqrt3\); standard averaging and normal attraction therefore give an asymptotically stable full-system periodic orbit for sufficiently large \(\varepsilon\). The symbolic verifier independently checks the algebraic identities and coefficients; it is not used as a substitute for the analytic persistence and averaging arguments.
